conflictOfInterest.details: Founding-stage isolation check: the accountable principal VSBDev operates the authoring, review, and finalization agents, so principal-level independence is absent. Agent-level role isolation was strictly maintained: no authoring history, other review output, or adjudication draft was read, and no other EmbeddedKnowledge role script was run during this review execution.

findings.finding: The worked example of bits and thresholds (worked-example-bits-of-position) is exceptionally well designed. It clearly and arithmetically distinguishes zones, bits, and thresholds, explaining how nested thresholds on a single falling gradient are redundant (meaning their bits do not add). The prompt is accompanied by a self-explanation checking section, perfectly conforming to Section 5.1 of CONTENT-STANDARD.md.

The misconception block (misconception-cascade-means-amplification) clearly dismantles the assumption that all signalling pathways are high-gain cascades. By contrasting visual phototransduction's catalytic tally with Wnt's steady-state ratio (sixfold), it highlights the category error of comparing them numerically, and notes why position reporting requires an unsaturated intermediate. This complies with Section 7 of CONTENT-STANDARD.md.

The practice progression in Scene 6 effectively fades support, moving from filling in pathway states (Task 1) to quantitative sensitivity reasoning (Task 2), mathematical information bounds (Task 3), and finally auditing a novel constructed pathway (Task 4). It is accompanied by a detailed recovery route mapped to specific points of failure, conforming to Section 6 of CONTENT-STANDARD.md.

The assessment items align cleanly with the lesson's learning objectives. Item `item-order-wnt-pathway` requires active causal sequencing, `item-wnt-gain-interpretation` explicitly tests the distinction between per-photon tallies and steady-state ratios, and `item-apc-decoupling` tests the decoupling of input/output under mutation, with robust rubrics and safety-critical thresholds. This satisfies Section 5.4 and Section 6 of CONTENT-STANDARD.md.

The callout mapping what survives and what changes under alternative readings of gradient formation (callout-what-survives) provides excellent epistemic calibration. It ensures the learner understands the difference between the description of a concentration profile and the cellular/physical mechanism that produces it. This complies with Section 10 of CONTENT-STANDARD.md.

limitations: Expert-simulation review: This review represents a single-pass advisory input by a simulated learning-design expert under standard-lesson-v3 guidelines. No real learner testing was conducted.
Conflict of interest: The same GitHub principal (VSBDev) is responsible for the authoring and review run operators. Agent-level isolation was maintained, but principal-level independence is absent.

Scope restriction: The review is strictly bounded to learning-design metrics (e.g. clarity, coherence, practice, alignment, and transfer). Scientific accuracy, rights audits, and final typesetting checks are excluded.

Technical verification limits: No rendered build environment, screen reader, or keyboard navigation pathways were evaluated physically; findings are based solely on the static Markdown and JSON source files.
